drivingQuestion: Does 'types of a meal offering' obligate one offering or two?
outcomeNote: the mishna proof is cancelled; the dilemma remains open

segments.he: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר ״מִינֵי״, תַּרְתֵּי קָאָמַר, וּמַאי ״מִנְחָה״? (דְּכוּלַּהּ) מְנָחוֹת נָמֵי ״מִנְחָה״ מִיקַּרְיָין, דִּכְתִיב ״וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הַמִּנְחָה״.
segments.en: The Gemara explains the dilemma: Perhaps it should be reasoned that «since he said: Types,» in the plural, apparently «he was saying» that he intends to bring «two» meal offerings. «And» if so, «what» is the reason he used the singular word: «Meal offering?» He used it «because the entire» category of «meal offerings is also referred to as: Meal offering,» in the singular, «as it is written» in the verse: «“And this is the law of the meal offering:» The sons of Aaron shall offer it before the Lord, in front of the altar” (Leviticus 6:7).

segments.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר ״מִנְחָה״, חֲדָא מִנְחָה קָאָמַר, וּמַאי ״מִינֵי מִנְחָה״? הָכִי קָאָמַר: ״מִמִּינֵי מִנְחָה חֲדָא מִנְחָה עֲלַי״.
segments.en: «Or perhaps» it should be reasoned that «since he said: Meal offering,» in the singular, apparently «he was saying» that he intends to bring only «one meal offering. And» if so, «what» did he mean by using the plural phrase: «Types of a meal offering? This» is what «he was saying: Of» the various «types of a meal offering,» it is incumbent «upon me» to bring «one.»

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״מִנְחָה״ ״מִין מִנְחָה״ – יָבִיא אַחַת, הָא ״מִינֵי מִנְחָה״ – שְׁתַּיִם.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» a proof that his intent is to bring two meal offerings, from that which is stated in the mishna: If one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring «a meal offering,» or: It is incumbent upon me to bring «a type of meal offering, he must bring one. This» indicates that if he said: «Types of a meal offering,» he must bring «two.»

segments.he: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: ״מְנָחוֹת״, ״מִין מְנָחוֹת״ – יָבִיא שְׁתַּיִם, הָא ״מִינֵי מִנְחָה״ – חֲדָא. אֶלָּא, מֵהָא לֵיכָּא לְמִשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this proof. «Say the latter clause:» If one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring «meal offerings,» or: It is incumbent upon me to bring «meal offerings of» a certain «type, he must bring two. This» indicates that if he says: «Types of a meal offering,» he must bring only «one. Rather, no» inference is «to be learned from this» mishna, as the potential inferences are contradictory.

moves.summary: side one: 'types' means two; 'meal offering' is a collective term
side two: 'meal offering' means one, of the types
inference from the mishna's first clause: two

moves.about: the latter clause yields the opposite inference, so the mishna proves nothing

moves.summary: nothing can be inferred from the mishna

edges.about: all meal offerings are called 'meal offering' in the singular
the mishna's singular clause implies 'types of a meal offering' requires two
the mishna's first clause as proof
from 'a type of meal offering – one' it follows 'types of a meal offering – two'
the latter clause yields the opposite inference, so the mishna proves nothing
